match.reason: The closest bank point, phys-displacement-velocity-acceleration, is written for Victorian Units 1 and 2 and centres on displacement, average velocity and the distance-displacement distinction, and it never defines speed as distance over time, so it is broader and at a higher depth than this Year 10 point.

draft.title: Speed, velocity and acceleration
card: Speed
how far an object travels in a given time. Speed = distance ÷ time, so 300 m in 60 s is 5 m/s.
Velocity
speed in a given direction, such as 5 m/s north. Speed has a size only. Velocity has a size and a direction.
Acceleration
how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time taken, measured in m/s².
Velocity changes if the speed changes, the direction changes, or both. So an object moving at a steady speed around a bend is accelerating.
draft.remember: Velocity is speed with a direction. Acceleration is how fast velocity changes.

a.q: Which of these gives a velocity, not just a speed?
opts: 12 m/s east
12 m/s
12 m in 1 s
12 m/s²
a.why: Velocity needs a size and a direction, and only 12 m/s east gives both. 12 m/s is a speed because it has no direction. 12 m/s² is a unit of acceleration.
a.clue: Look for the option that says which way.

b.q: A cyclist in Hobart rides a bend at a steady 8 m/s. Her direction changes the whole way round. What is true of her motion?
opts: Her velocity changes, so she is accelerating
Her velocity is steady, so she is not accelerating
Her speed changes, so she is accelerating
Her acceleration is zero, as her speed is steady
b.why: Velocity includes direction, so a change in direction is a change in velocity. That means she is accelerating even though her speed stays at 8 m/s. Steady speed alone does not mean steady velocity.
b.clue: Does velocity depend on direction as well as speed?

b.best: Her velocity changes, so she is accelerating

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for the option that says which way' gives the answer away. Only one option includes a direction, so a student can pick it without understanding velocity.
Why (a) calls 12 m/s² 'a unit of acceleration'. It is a value of acceleration; the unit is m/s². The why also never explains why '12 m in 1 s' is wrong.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. Question a's clue all but names the answer, and its why wrongly calls 12 m/s² a unit rather than a value of acceleration.
